messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: High 5xx rate observed for tenant=lyra-prod (VPC us-east-1). metric=5xx_rate > 4% (rolling 5m). Affected model: gptx-1.2-quant. Paging oncall: @sara.

cs-rob: Customer (Lyra) reports degraded responses and some invalid generations. They say this started ~10m ago. Lyra is on dedicated pool lyra-dedicated-3.

sara: taking it — /ack @incident-bot. pinging eng-runtime and eng-ml for triage. :eyes:

michael: looking at runtime logs now, seeing repeated kernel fallbacks and KV cache thrashing. latency + errors correlate with longer prompt lengths. hypothesis: quantized kernel fallback path causing decode errors.

ali: quick ML note — we pushed fix in gptx v1.2.1 for a quant fallback edge-case, but Lyra had pinned to v1.2.0 last month. sounds related.

jen: ops action: isolating tenant traffic to prepare safe switch. will apply routing override to route Lyra to safe variant gptx-1.2-safe-v2 in the dedicated pool. doing canary 10% first.

michael: before switching — what are perf differences for safe-v2 vs pinned quant? need to set CS expectations.

cs-rob: I'll tell customer it's a temporary switch, expect small latency increase (100-300ms) but correctness should return.

sara: handoff note — I'm on pager until 02:00Z, handoff to @mike_night then. keeping watch until canary proves green.

ali: recommended approach: tenant-level pin override (no global deploy). set model_pin to gptx-1.2-safe-v2 for lyra. that leaves other tenants untouched.

michael: executing tenant pin via admin API now.

michael: ```json
PATCH /admin/tenants/lyra/config
{ "model_pin": "gptx-1.2-safe-v2", "pin_reason": "runtime_quant_fallback_5xx" }
```

jen: applied -> 200 OK. routing table updated: lyra -> lyra-dedicated-3:gptx-1.2-safe-v2. Canary=10% started.

incident-bot: Canary update: 10% traffic to gptx-1.2-safe-v2. Observed 5xx_rate dropping from 4.6% -> 0.3% in first 2 mins. :white_check_mark:

cs-rob: pinged customer support channel. Lyra rep (tina) says they're seeing improved outputs but a handful of requests slower.

sara: ramp plan: 10% -> 50% over 3m, then 100% over 5m if metrics stable. adding guardrail: abort if 5xx_rate > 1% or p95 latency > baseline + 500ms.

michael: preparing rollback snippet if perf tradeoff unacceptable.

michael: ```
# rollback to remove tenant pin
PATCH /admin/tenants/lyra/config
{ "model_pin": null }
```

ali: follow-up: schedule model onboard for lyra to v1.2.1 (we need explicit customer opt-in due to pinned state). We'll run the quant kernel validation on lyra prompt set in staging.

tina: Thanks for the quick action. Can you confirm ETA to full recovery and any user-facing note we should send?

cs-rob: ETA ~8-12 minutes to full recovery based on canary. Draft note: "We've applied a temporary model variant to mitigate decoding errors; no customer data was affected. We're monitoring and will follow up with a post-incident summary."

sara: creating follow-up tasks: add runbook entry for tenant pin fallback, add alert for pinned-tenants-with-old-versions.

jen: logged incident mitigation to ticket INC-2365, attached routing change diff and kernel logs.

incident-bot: ALERT: Canary ramp to 100% completed, thresholds OK. 5xx_rate steady at 0.2% for 10m. Marking incident as resolved if no regressions.

mike_night: ack takeover — monitoring dashboards and traces now. will page if anything spikes.

cs-rob: Lyra confirmed service healthy on their side. Closing customer loop. :white_check_mark:

sara: post-incident blameless note: root cause = pinned older quant model (v1.2.0) + edge-case kernel fallback under longer prompts. Mitigation = tenant pin override to safe variant + plan to onboard v1.2.1.

ali: next steps: coordinate with Lyra for scheduled upgrade to v1.2.1, run quant kernel tests, add automated alert detecting tenants pinned to older vulnerable builds.

jen: done — adding follow-up epics and PRs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: alert closed at ts=2365000899. :tada:

cs-rob: thanks team. I'll schedule post-incident review with Lyra and Engineering to agree on upgrade windows.

mike_night: signing off.

(some reactions: :thumbsup: from cs-rob, :eyes: from ali, :rocket: from jen)
